answer: In an agent economy routing freight across tundra, a gale closing a bridge may trigger a vote on rerouting payments. Voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, not the number of agent accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake identities still buys only 100 tokens of influence. To gain more power, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere.
